channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Hex local voice dictation: hold a key, speak, and it pastes
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Hex is free, open-source voice dictation that runs entirely on your machine — hold a key, speak, let go, and your words paste into any app. This guide installs it, runs a first dictation, swaps speech models, and drives it from the terminal.

item.title: OpenAI pledges to pay its own data-centre power bills in a National Community Compact
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Two days after midterm voters backed curbs on data-centre expansion, OpenAI published a National Community Compact promising to cover the full cost of its campuses' electricity, publish site-level water and power figures, and stop asking local officials to sign NDAs. The catch: the promises are voluntary, and OpenAI grades its own homework.

item.title: Charts your coding agent can actually draw: hands-on with Microsoft Flint 1.0
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Your coding agent can write a chart spec, but the chart it draws is usually wrong — wrong type, unreadable labels, no interaction. Microsoft’s Flint 1.0 is a visualization language built for agents: one semantic spec compiles to five backends, with 14 themes and 23 interaction presets — this guide wires in its MCP server, renders a first chart, and compiles the same spec three ways, every step verified.

item.title: Theo, a wheeled humanoid robot, restocked a Zurich supermarket on camera — and Reddit is checking the 400-items-an-hour claim
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A video of Theo, a wheeled humanoid robot, restocking shelves in a Zurich supermarket spread fast on r/singularity: 400 items an hour, overnight, in the dark. The top comments did the math — and the poster conceded the number comes with conditions.

item.title: Meta buys Conductor, the multi-agent coding startup — and its cloud service shuts down November 20
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Meta has acquired Conductor, the startup that lets developers run several AI coding agents in parallel workspaces. The team joins Meta Superintelligence Labs — and Conductor Cloud goes read-only on November 13, then shuts down on November 20, with user data deletion to follow.

item.title: Reverse-engineer any video with rea-video: tell filmed, AI, and code apart, shot by shot
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: JuneYaooo/rea-video (3,681 stars on November 7, 2026, Apache-2.0) reverse-engineers any video shot by shot — filmed, AI-generated, 3D, or built in code — and hands you a remake plan: what to film, what to generate, what to code. It runs in Claude Code or Codex, needs only ffmpeg and Python 3.10+, and its offline tools-only mode is free. Hands-on: the install, your first breakdown, reading the report, and planning the remake.

item.title: Data centers pay 40% of one Virginia county’s taxes — and Reddit says that’s exactly why nobody else can copy it
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: A 50-second WSJ clip of Loudoun County’s economic development chief went viral on r/singularity: $1.2 billion a year in tax revenue, about 40% of the county’s total, from data centers on 3% of its land. The top comment’s verdict: Loudoun is the exception, not the model.

item.title: Horizon hands-on: your own AI news radar, from install to your first daily briefing
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Horizon is a self-hosted Python tool that pulls Hacker News, RSS, Reddit and GitHub into one place, scores every item with a model you choose, and writes a ranked daily briefing. This guide installs it, wires up a model, and produces a real briefing — every command verified.

item.title: Build an MCP server in TypeScript: your own tools, wired into Claude Code
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: MCP's TypeScript SDK split into server and client packages in v2. This guide builds a real notes server with the new API — four tools, a resource, and a prompt — tests it with a real client and the Inspector, and wires it into Claude Code.

item.title: Orkas hands-on: put a 16-agent AI team to work on your own desktop
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Orkas is an MIT-licensed, local-first desktop app where a Commander coordinates 16 specialist agents plus Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes. This guide installs v2026.11.4, checks the Linux source path, wires up a model, and runs a real multi-agent launch package.

item.title: The AI labs agree on how to grade a jailbreak: Frontier Model Forum releases a shared cyber-risk rating
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Microsoft and Amazon now share one yardstick for rating AI jailbreaks: four scores, five risk bands, and a public comment period that runs to December 21.

item.title: Your own ChatGPT, with a computer attached: hands-on with Open WebUI 0.13
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Open WebUI 0.13.0 turns the self-hosted chat front end into a full workspace: your model gets a desktop, a browser, and Git beside the chat. This guide installs 0.13.0, connects a local model, builds a knowledge base, and walks the new computer-use features — install, chat, and RAG verified end to end.

item.title: Agent Autoloop hands-on: your coding agents keep working in the background
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Agent Autoloop turns Claude Code, Codex, and other command-line agents into a background loop: it dispatches work on a schedule or a webhook, exits while it waits for your call, and resumes the same conversation when you answer. This guide installs v1.6.3, runs the guided trial, and wires a morning-brief rule.

item.title: Claude Code blocked a developer from debugging his own software — and Reddit says it's happening to everyone
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A developer asked Claude Code to fix a browser reconnect bug in his own project. It refused, calling the request reverse engineering — and the thread that followed says he's far from the only one.

item.title: Month-long coding sessions on a 100K context window: hands-on with billion-context
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: billion-context is a local proxy that sits between your coding agent and the model API, folding consumed conversation into summaries the model itself writes — so one session can run for weeks. This guide installs 0.1.212, proves the proxy rewrites requests, and shows how to read its cache report.

item.title: Run your own AI security operations center: hands-on with AiSOC
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: AiSOC is an open-source, self-hosted security operations center that triages alerts with a local AI agent — no API keys, no cloud. This guide runs its offline sandbox in under a minute, walks a real alert through the investigation funnel, and maps the path to the full deployment.

item.title: Anthropic's IPO price tag slides toward $1.2 trillion as investors balk after the AI selloff
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Investors are now discussing a $1.2 trillion to $1.3 trillion valuation for Anthropic's IPO, down from as high as $2 trillion in early October, after a sharp AI stock selloff — and the roadshow planned for next week is suddenly in doubt.

item.title: US intelligence memo reportedly links Nvidia's Jensen Huang to alleged Chinese spy
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: US intelligence believes Nvidia chief Jensen Huang was romantically involved with an executive Washington says was recruited by China's spy agency, according to the Financial Times and the New York Times. Nothing is proven — and Congress now wants answers.

item.title: Drive a real browser from your terminal: hands-on with agent-browser, Vercel's CLI for AI agents
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: agent-browser is Vercel's Rust CLI for driving a real browser from the shell: snapshot a page as text, act on element refs, and automate anything a human can click. This guide installs 0.41.2, runs the core loop, extracts live data, drives forms, and wires up MCP — every command verified.

item.title: Octop 1.0.3, hands-on: upgrade your self-hosted AI assistant and build your first expert team
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Tencent's Octop has doubled to 11,753 stars since our first guide, and versions 1.0.2 and 1.0.3 add expert teams, a second-instance cloud bridge, memory you can edit by hand, and an agent MCP gateway. Back up, run octop update, and put the new features to work — every command verified against the current README and release notes.

item.title: GPT-6.1 Terra, hands-on: visual reasoning, structured outputs, and tools with the Responses API
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: OpenAI’s GPT-6.1 Terra is the fast, cheap vision model of the GPT-6 family — $1 per million input tokens, a 1.05M-token context window, and tool calling through the Responses API. This guide makes your first call, feeds it a photo, forces structured JSON out of it, and wires up web search and your own functions — every snippet verified against the official docs.

item.title: Shield AI buys radar maker Echodyne for $5.3B and raises $2.5B at a $28.8B valuation
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Shield AI is buying Kirkland radar maker Echodyne in a deal worth up to $5.3 billion, pairing its autonomy software with the sensors that spot drones — and raising $2.5 billion to pay for it, at a valuation more than double its March mark.

item.title: Your AI agents as chat contacts: hands-on with OpenMausBot, the open-source Grok Bot alternative
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: OpenMausBot turns Claude Code, Codex and Grok into contacts in a chat app — each with its own model, computer and apps. This guide installs the CLI, starts the server, builds a team from a file, and shows exactly where the login gate is. Every command verified.

item.title: A team of 8 built a GTA-style Bangkok in 8 days with its own AI-native engine — and Reddit is checking how much of it the AI really did
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Eight days of in-engine footage shows a GTA-style Bangkok — tuk-tuks, water-cannon trucks and Komodo dragons — built with the team’s own AI-native engine, Oriverse. Reddit’s top comments are equal parts impressed and unconvinced about how much of it the AI really did.

item.title: From one page to a whole crawl: hands-on with Scrapling, the 99K-star Python scraping framework
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Scrapling packs fast HTTP fetching, a stealth browser, adaptive parsing, spiders, a CLI, an MCP server and an agent skill into one Python library. This guide installs 0.5.1, scrapes a real site three ways, crawls 100 quotes into JSON, and wires it into an AI agent — every command verified.
